Yes, this is still broken in `webpack@5.0.0-beta.0`
I updated the reproduction to `webpack@5.0.0-beta.12` and this still persists

What if foo1.mjs exports morethan `foo`, like `foo` and `bar`, while foo2.mjs exports `foo` and `baz`, while foo.mjs wants to export `foo` and `baz` from foo2.mjs and `bar` from foo1.mjs?

This is a catch IMO, re-exporting just can have such conflicts that cannot be solved simply by throwing an error.

issue.title: track reexport target during providedExports analysis

repository.name: webpack
repository.description: A bundler for javascript and friends. Packs many modules into a few bundled assets. Code Splitting allows for loading parts of the application on demand. Through "loaders", modules can be CommonJs, AMD, ES6 modules, CSS, Images, JSON, Coffeescript, LESS, ... and your custom stuff.
